---
title: "House Varen"
subtitle: "Expansion Era (~15,000–18,000 SD)"
---


Proto-Great House and colonial charter corporation active during the Expansion Era (~15,000–18,400 SD). Based on Vethara. One of the entities that will eventually consolidate into the 12 Great Houses of the Imperial Era, though its precise lineage forward is not yet determined.

## Character

House Varen's identity is colonial expansion — rights acquisition, settlement logistics, long-range viability assessment. Not a military House. Not a technology House. A patient one. Varen's competitive advantage is the willingness to fund 30-year voyages to worlds with low glamour and high projected return. Their portfolio is populated with "generation two worlds" — places that will not be profitable for 80 years but will be indispensable in 200.

Aldric Vonn is their Mission Director for the Threshold voyage. He is competent, well-resourced, and representative of Varen's organizational culture: methodical, risk-averse on macro questions, willing to accept calculated micro-risks on cost decisions that are unlikely to matter. The passenger pod procurement decision — single-use spec instead of multi-cycle, saving approximately 40% of pod cost — is characteristic of that calculus. It was not irresponsible. It was normal.

## Colonial Operations

At the time of the Threshold voyage, House Varen has launched approximately 12 colony ships in the preceding century. Most are en route or have arrived and established early-stage settlements. Varen maintains a colonial operations office on Vethara Station, where the Threshold departed.

The colonial charter framework — under which Varen holds rights to Aranda and is legally responsible for the settlement — is administered by the CGSS. If the Threshold fails, the charter reverts. If it succeeds, Varen receives a percentage of Aranda's economic output for 150 years. This is the economics of the Expansion Era: patient capital, generational returns, Houses as the organizational unit of civilization.
